title: Bytes to hex and back
description:
Write two helpers:

- `toHex(bytes)` takes a `Uint8Array` and returns its bytes as two-digit lower-case hex separated by spaces: `toHex(new Uint8Array([0, 255, 16]))` is `"00 ff 10"`. An empty array gives `""`.
- `fromHex(text)` does the reverse and returns a `Uint8Array`. Spaces anywhere are ignored, upper case is fine, and anything that is not an even number of hex digits throws a `SyntaxError`.
hints: `Array.from(bytes, b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"))` turns each byte into two hex digits (lesson 8.01).
Remove the spaces first with `text.replace(/\s+/g, "")`, check the length is even and only hex digits remain, then `parseInt(pair, 16)` each pair.
